title: Working for Vee-Jay and the Sunset budget line at United Artists
summary: Randy Wood hired Lee at Vee-Jay, which had the first Beatle records; after it closed he ran UA's $1.99 Sunset reissue line.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: See, what they will do is they won't pay you, but

they'll pay all the big companies. You know, they'll pay the big companies, so you don't have much of a shot, so I don't think -- and after I fooled with my company a little while, then the President, Randy Wood, called me at VeeJay and wanted me to come to work for VeeJay records.
Now I had never worked for a record company in my life, and so ...

Yeah, there's one black and one white. Well, this was the black one -- VeeJay, right. So after I was there about a year and 3 months, you know, remember VeeJay had all the first Beatle records; all the first Beatle records, because Randy made the deal, which was a heck of a deal he made.

But after a year and 3 months, they closed down and moved back to Chicago. And from there, I went to UA, which is Liberty Records, and I ran the budget line there, which was called Sunset. There was a Sunset label, and I run the budget line -- it was $1.99 album, and so I had to package it all together, which was really great experience.
And while I was working there ..,
Were these new recordings or were they reissues?
No, they were reissues. And it was great experience, because it gave me a chance to meet all the different publishers, because I used to talk to them about rates all over the country.
